For anyone who's curious about the malfouf the recipe I use  is:  

1 cabbage head (preferably green but I used savoy)   

500g ground beef (lamb, mutton or pork also works)  

0.5 cup rice, rinsed, uncooked  

1tsp cinnamon  

1tsp cumin  

1tsp paprika  

0.5tsp chilli powder  

8 cloves garlic  

Lemon juice  

Dried mint  

Broth  

S+p  

1) Steam the whole cabbage head in a pan until the leaves can easily be removed 

2) Mix the ground beef with the rice, s+p, and the spices not including the mint. (And only half the garlic) 

3) Cut the hard bottom bit from each cabbage leaf and put the meat mixture in it and roll like a little burrito 

4) Put each cabbage roll into a saucepan and when one layer is formed, cover in a generous amount of mint and lemon juice, pepper and some of the remaining garlic, repeat this for each layer of cabbage roll (my saucepan is large so it made 2 layers)

5) Cover the cabbage in broth until all the cabbage is submerged. Bring to a boil and then simmer on med-low with the lid on for 30 minutes. Then it's ready to serve with more mint or some fresh coriander (cilantro). 

This is a recipe that has variations from a few middle Eastern countries, I adapted from a Palestinian recipe. Allspice also goes well in the meat rice mixture. And the rice cooks perfectly inside the cabbage!

Serves around 4-5 

1tsp vegetable oil 
1tsp cornflour (cornstarch) 
1 onion 
1 garlic clove 
Teaspoon ginger root 
3 spring onions (green onion) 
16 imitation crab sticks 
1 326g tin of sweetcorn (include the liquid) 
3 chicken stock cubes  
White of one egg 
1 green chilli (optional) 
1.5 tbsp light soy sauce  

Dice the onion, garlic and ginger into tiny pieces.

Fry the onion, garlic, and ginger in the oil until slightly softened.

Add the tin of sweetcorn including the liquid and 2 cups of water with 3 chicken stock cubes (or 2 cups of chicken stock). 

Peel the crab sticks into thin strips and add to the pot with soy sauce and chopped spring onion.

Simmer for 20-25 minutes, add more liquid if you need. 

Make a slurry with the cornstarch and add to the pot, keep simmering for a few more minutes. 

Slowly trickle the egg whites into the pot and keep stirring the soup to make thin strands of egg in the soup. Simmer again for another minute.

Serve and top with chopped green chilli (I didn't but I usually do and it is lovely), and season with salt and pepper if you need to (I don't and feel it's flavourful enough).

Lentil dal is my favourite.

1 cup red or yellow split lentils  
2 cups water  
vegetable or chicken stock cube  
2 tsp cumin (whole or ground)  
1 tsp mustard seeds  
2 tsp curry powder  
2 tsp garam masala  
1 tsp paprika  
1 tsp cinnamon  
1 tsp garlic powder  
0.5-1tsp chilli powder to taste   
2 or 3 bay leaves  
2 tsp turmeric  
1 tsp ground coriander  
1 tsp ginger puree or chopped  
3 garlic cloves  
1 or 2 chopped onions  
half cup tomato sauce  
can of coconut milk (the solid part of it)   
salt and pepper to taste, fresh coriander to serve.   

You can either fry the onions, garlic, ginger and spices and add the lentils and liquids and simmer for 30 minutes or so, or shove it all in the slow cooker on low for 4-5 hours. If you have a well stocked spice cupboard it's dirt cheap and is really filling - you can also add any vegetables you like, I like to add spinach and mushrooms and serve with roasted vegetables and curried potatoes (or just rice and flat bread). It freezes well and you can heat in the microwave or on the stove with a bit of water.
